rachel: flagging a regression on long-context (>1k tokens) runs with the new postnorm int4 profile. repeating tokens after ~600 tokens, not seen in fp16. cc @tom @li

Tom: can you share quick repro + numbers?

rachel: repro: run `long_dialog_eval` on model-x with `postnorm-int4-v3`. Observed: token_repeat_rate 0.39 (fp16 0.10), perplexity +8%. Minimal steps:
```
calibrate(model-x, mode='postnorm', bits=4, samples=120)
run_eval(model-x-quant, suite='long_dialog_eval')
```

li: sounds like cumulative residual bias across layers. Are we folding biases pre-quant?

rachel: yes — we fold pre-attn bias into weights, then quantize. Hypothesis: asymmetric scales + folding introduce small per-layer offsets that accumulate across many tokens. Not the old headwise clipping bug.

Tom: options: 1) full recalibration with bias-correction (slow) 2) runtime offset shim (cheap) 3) route long requests to int8/fp8. Tradeoffs?

li: prefer runtime shim: store per-layer float32 offset vector computed on a small calib set and subtract after dequantize. Overhead: one vector add per layer. Add gating: `min_layer_energy` and `max_abs_offset` to avoid overcorrection.

rachel: agreed. telemetry suggested: `quant_offset_mean[layer]`, `quant_offset_std[layer]`, and `longctx_quality_delta` from shadowing. If mean > 0.025 or std spikes -> auto-failover to int8.

canary-bot: Canary scheduled: shadow-int4-offset-shim on prod-dedicated @ 06/10 03:00 UTC (3% mirror sampling)

Tom: lifecycle notes: offsets must be versioned and invalidated on model weight updates. Add `offset_version` + `offset_created_at` to profile metadata. Lint that blocks enabling shim without offsets.

li: tests: synthetic accumulation test (simulate steady positive residual across tokens) and perf smoke (<2% throughput loss expected). Also add unit test ensuring clamp behavior when offsets exceed threshold.

rachel: action items: rachel -> implement shim + unit tests, tom -> telemetry + lint, li -> canary config. ETA 1 week. Filing RFC follow-up with playbook & rollback steps.
